RagShortTexts: The Battle of Durbe in 1260 crushed the Teutonic and Livonian Orders, slaying 150 elite knights.

Variants.Content: On 13 July 1260 the Battle of Durbe shattered the military core of the Teutonic and Livonian Orders. The army marched against Samogitian pagans near Lake Durbe, but the Curonian auxiliary levies in its ranks defected at the decisive moment. Pagan warriors then closed around the host, and the Livonian Landmeister Burkhard von Hornhausen, the Prussian Marshal and some 150 elite knights fell in the fighting. The loss of those knights and their horses left the crusader states without a reserve. A defeat of that scale was hard to repair, because each knight came with years of training and a retinue to sustain him.

Durbe triggered a pan-Baltic conflagration. Emboldened pagans stripped knightly plate and arms, and coordinated uprisings spread from Prussia to Livonia, threatening to drive the crusaders into the sea. Lords who had pledged service to the Order now had to decide whether to hold their castles or open negotiations with the rebels.

Heavy destriers floundered in lakeside bogs while pagan war clubs smashed great helms. When Curonian auxiliaries turned their spears against the Order, panic ran down the line. Men who had trusted the auxiliaries as flank guards found themselves cut off, and the flower of the crusaders was butchered in the reeds.
